verses.kjv: The words of Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah. And it came to pass in the month Chisleu, in the twentieth year, as I was in Shushan the palace,
verses.modern: The words of Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, while I was at the citadel of Shushan,

verses.kjv: That Hanani, one of my brethren, came, he and certain men of Judah; and I asked them concerning the Jews that had escaped, which were left of the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem.
verses.modern: Hanani, one of my brothers, arrived with some men from Judah. I asked them about the Jews who had survived the exile, and about Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And they said unto me, The remnant that are left of the captivity there in the province are in great affliction and reproach: the wall of Jerusalem also is broken down, and the gates thereof are burned with fire.
verses.modern: They said to me, "The survivors who are left from the exile in the province are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept, and mourned certain days, and fasted, and prayed before the God of heaven,
verses.modern: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept. I mourned for several days, fasting and praying before the God of heaven.

verses.kjv: And said, I beseech thee, O LORD God of heaven, the great and terrible God, that keepeth covenant and mercy for them that love him and observe his commandments:
verses.modern: I said, "LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, Who keeps His covenant and mercy with those who love Him and keep His commandments —

verses.kjv: Let thine ear now be attentive, and thine eyes open, that thou mayest hear the prayer of thy servant, which I pray before thee now, day and night, for the children of Israel thy servants, and confess the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against thee: both I and my father's house have sinned.
verses.modern: let Your ear be attentive and Your eyes open, to hear the prayer Your servant prays before You day and night for the people of Israel. I confess the sins we have committed against You — yes, I and my father's house have sinned.

verses.kjv: We have dealt very corruptly against thee, and have not kept the commandments, nor the statutes, nor the judgments, which thou commandedst thy servant Moses.
verses.modern: We have acted very corruptly against you. We have not kept the commandments, statutes, and judgments you commanded your servant Moses.

verses.kjv: Remember, I beseech thee, the word that thou commandedst thy servant Moses, saying, If ye transgress, I will scatter you abroad among the nations:
verses.modern: Please remember the word you commanded your servant Moses: 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the peoples;

verses.kjv: But if ye turn unto me, and keep my commandments, and do them; though there were of you cast out unto the uttermost part of the heaven, yet will I gather them from thence, and will bring them unto the place that I have chosen to set my name there.
verses.modern: but if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, then even if your exiles are at the farthest horizon, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place I have chosen for my name to dwell.'

verses.kjv: Now these are thy servants and thy people, whom thou hast redeemed by thy great power, and by thy strong hand.
verses.modern: These are your servants and your people, whom you have redeemed by your great power and your strong hand.

verses.kjv: O LORD, I beseech thee, let now thine ear be attentive to the prayer of thy servant, and to the prayer of thy servants, who desire to fear thy name: and prosper, I pray thee, thy servant this day, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man. For I was the king's cupbearer.
verses.modern: O Lord, please let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayer of your servants who delight to fear your name. Give your servant success today, and grant him favor in the presence of this man." For I was the king's cupbearer.

chapters.summary: Nehemiah, cupbearer to King Artaxerxes in Susa, received word from his brother Hanani that Jerusalem’s walls were broken down and its gates burned. Nehemiah wept, fasted, and prayed, confessing Israel’s sins and asking God for favor before the king.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that wine was before him: and I took up the wine, and gave it unto the king. Now I had not been beforetime sad in his presence.
verses.modern: In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, wine was before him. I took up the wine and gave it to the king. I had never before been sad in his presence.

verses.kjv: Wherefore the king said unto me, Why is thy countenance sad, seeing thou art not sick? this is nothing else but sorrow of heart. Then I was very sore afraid,
verses.modern: So the king said to me, "Why is your countenance sad, since you are not sick? This can only be sadness of heart." Then I was very much afraid.

verses.kjv: And said unto the king, Let the king live for ever: why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' sepulchres, lieth waste, and the gates thereof are consumed with fire?
verses.modern: I said to the king, "May the king live forever! Why should my countenance not be sad, when the city where my fathers are buried lies in ruins, and its gates have been destroyed by fire?"

verses.kjv: Then the king said unto me, For what dost thou make request? So I prayed to the God of heaven.
verses.modern: The king said to me, "What do you want?" So I prayed to the God of heaven,

verses.kjv: And I said unto the king, If it please the king, and if thy servant have found favour in thy sight, that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers' sepulchres, that I may build it.
verses.modern: I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, please send me to Judah, to the city of my fathers' tombs, so that I may rebuild it."

verses.kjv: And the king said unto me, (the queen also sitting by him,) For how long shall thy journey be? and when wilt thou return? So it pleased the king to send me; and I set him a time.
verses.modern: The king said to me (with the queen sitting beside him), "How long will your journey take, and when will you return?" It pleased the king to send me. I gave him a time.

verses.kjv: Moreover I said unto the king, If it please the king, let letters be given me to the governors beyond the river, that they may convey me over till I come into Judah;
verses.modern: I also said to the king, "If it pleases the king, let letters be given to me for the governors of the region beyond the River, so that they will let me pass through until I reach Judah;

verses.kjv: And a letter unto Asaph the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the palace which appertained to the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall enter into. And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.
verses.modern: a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest, so that he will give me timber to make beams for the gates of the fortress of the temple, for the city wall, and for the house I will occupy." The king granted these requests, for the good hand of my God was on me.

verses.kjv: Then I came to the governors beyond the river, and gave them the king's letters. Now the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with me.
verses.modern: Then I came to the governors of the region beyond the River and gave them the king's letters. The king had also sent army officers and horsemen with me.

verses.kjv: When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.
verses.modern: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard this, it troubled them greatly that someone had come to seek the welfare of the people of Israel.

verses.kjv: So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.
verses.modern: So I came to Jerusalem and was there three days.

verses.kjv: And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither told I any man what my God had put in my heart to do at Jerusalem: neither was there any beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon.
verses.modern: Then I arose in the night, I and a few men with me. I had not told anyone what my God had put in my heart to do for Jerusalem. There was no animal with me but the one I was riding.

verses.kjv: And I went out by night by the gate of the valley, even before the dragon well, and to the dung port, and viewed the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and the gates thereof were consumed with fire.
verses.modern: I went out by night through the Valley Gate, past the Dragon Spring, and to the Refuse Gate, inspecting the walls of Jerusalem that were broken down and its gates that had been destroyed by fire.

verses.kjv: Then I went on to the gate of the fountain, and to the king's pool: but there was no place for the beast that was under me to pass.
verses.modern: Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to pass through.

verses.kjv: Then went I up in the night by the brook, and viewed the wall, and turned back, and entered by the gate of the valley, and so returned.
verses.modern: So I went up in the night along the valley and inspected the wall, then turned back and entered through the Valley Gate, and returned.

verses.kjv: And the rulers knew not whither I went, or what I did; neither had I as yet told it to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the nobles, nor to the rulers, nor to the rest that did the work.
verses.modern: The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing. I had not yet told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or any of the others who would be doing the work.

verses.kjv: Then said I unto them, Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste, and the gates thereof are burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach.
verses.modern: Then I said to them, "You see the trouble we are in — how Jerusalem lies in ruins with its gates burned down. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem so that we will no longer be a disgrace."

verses.kjv: Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king's words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for this good work.
verses.modern: I also told them about the good hand of my God on me, and about the king's words that he had spoken to me. They said, "Let us rise up and build." So they committed themselves to the good work.

verses.kjv: But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, they laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What is this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?
verses.modern: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about it, they mocked and despised us, saying, "What is this thing you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"

verses.kjv: Then answered I them, and said unto them, The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.
verses.modern: I replied to them, "The God of heaven will give us success. We His servants will rise up and build. But you have no share, no right, and no claim in Jerusalem."

chapters.summary: The king noticed Nehemiah’s sadness and granted him letters and an escort to go to Jerusalem and rebuild the walls. Nehemiah inspected the ruined walls by night and rallied the people to build, despite the mockery of Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem.

verses.kjv: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brethren the priests, and they builded the sheep gate; they sanctified it, and set up the doors of it; even unto the tower of Meah they sanctified it, unto the tower of Hananeel.
verses.modern: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his fellow priests and built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set its doors in place, consecrating it as far as the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel.

verses.kjv: And next unto him builded the men of Jericho. And next to them builded Zaccur the son of Imri.
verses.modern: Next to him the men of Jericho built. And next to them Zaccur the son of Imri built.

verses.kjv: But the fish gate did the sons of Hassenaah build, who also laid the beams thereof, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof.
verses.modern: The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate; they laid its beams and set its doors, bolts, and bars in place.

verses.kjv: And next unto them repaired Meremoth the son of Urijah, the son of Koz. And next unto them repaired Meshullam the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabeel. And next unto them repaired Zadok the son of Baana.
verses.modern: Next to them Meremoth the son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, made repairs. Next to them Meshullam the son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, made repairs. Next to them Zadok the son of Baana made repairs.

verses.kjv: And next unto them the Tekoites repaired; but their nobles put not their necks to the work of their LORD.
verses.modern: Next to them the Tekoites made repairs, though their nobles would not stoop to serve their Lord.

verses.kjv: Moreover the old gate repaired Jehoiada the son of Paseah, and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah; they laid the beams thereof, and set up the doors thereof, and the locks thereof, and the bars thereof.
verses.modern: Jehoiada the son of Paseah and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah repaired the Jeshanah Gate; they laid its beams and set its doors, bolts, and bars in place.

verses.kjv: And next unto them repaired Melatiah the Gibeonite, and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon, and of Mizpah, unto the throne of the governor on this side the river.
verses.modern: Next to them Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite made repairs — the men of Gibeon and Mizpah — who were under the authority of the governor of the region beyond the River.

verses.kjv: Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths. Next unto him also repaired Hananiah the son of one of the apothecaries, and they fortified Jerusalem unto the broad wall.
verses.modern: Next to him Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs. Next to him Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs. They restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.

verses.kjv: And next unto them repaired Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of the half part of Jerusalem.
verses.modern: Next to them Rephaiah the son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.

verses.kjv: And next unto them repaired Jedaiah the son of Harumaph, even over against his house. And next unto him repaired Hattush the son of Hashabniah.
verses.modern: Next to them Jedaiah the son of Harumaph made repairs opposite his house. Next to him Hattush the son of Hashabneiah made repairs.

verses.kjv: Malchijah the son of Harim, and Hashub the son of Pahathmoab, repaired the other piece, and the tower of the furnaces.
verses.modern: Malchijah the son of Harim and Hasshub the son of Pahath-moab repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens.

verses.kjv: And next unto him repaired Shallum the son of Halohesh, the ruler of the half part of Jerusalem, he and his daughters.
verses.modern: Next to him Shallum the son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs — he and his daughters.

verses.kjv: The valley gate repaired Hanun, and the inhabitants of Zanoah; they built it, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof, and a thousand cubits on the wall unto the dung gate.
verses.modern: Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate. They rebuilt it and set its doors, bolts, and bars in place, and also repaired a thousand cubits of wall to the Refuse Gate.

verses.kjv: But the dung gate repaired Malchiah the son of Rechab, the ruler of part of Bethhaccerem; he built it, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof.
verses.modern: Malchijah the son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccerem, repaired the Refuse Gate. He rebuilt it and set its doors, bolts, and bars in place.

verses.kjv: But the gate of the fountain repaired Shallun the son of Colhozeh, the ruler of part of Mizpah; he built it, and covered it, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof, and the wall of the pool of Siloah by the king's garden, even unto the stairs that go down from the city of David.
verses.modern: Shallun the son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He rebuilt it, roofed it, and set its doors, bolts, and bars in place. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah near the king's garden, as far as the stairs that go down from the City of David.

verses.kjv: After him repaired Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of the half part of Bethzur, unto the place over against the sepulchres of David, and to the pool that was made, and unto the house of the mighty.
verses.modern: After him Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, made repairs as far as the tombs of David, and as far as the artificial pool and the House of the Warriors.

verses.kjv: After him repaired the Levites, Rehum the son of Bani. Next unto him repaired Hashabiah, the ruler of the half part of Keilah, in his part.
verses.modern: After him the Levites made repairs — Rehum the son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.

verses.kjv: After him repaired their brethren, Bavai the son of Henadad, the ruler of the half part of Keilah.
verses.modern: After him their fellow Levites made repairs — Bavvai the son of Henadad, ruler of the other half of the district of Keilah.

verses.kjv: And next to him repaired Ezer the son of Jeshua, the ruler of Mizpah, another piece over against the going up to the armoury at the turning of the wall.
verses.modern: Next to him Ezer the son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section opposite the ascent to the armory at the Angle.

verses.kjv: After him Baruch the son of Zabbai earnestly repaired the other piece, from the turning of the wall unto the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
verses.modern: After him Baruch the son of Zabbai diligently repaired another section, from the Angle to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.

verses.kjv: After him repaired Meremoth the son of Urijah the son of Koz another piece, from the door of the house of Eliashib even to the end of the house of Eliashib.
verses.modern: After him Meremoth the son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the door of Eliashib's house to the end of it.

verses.kjv: And after him repaired the priests, the men of the plain.
verses.modern: After him the priests, the men of the surrounding area, made repairs.

verses.kjv: After him repaired Benjamin and Hashub over against their house. After him repaired Azariah the son of Maaseiah the son of Ananiah by his house.
verses.modern: After them Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs opposite their house. After them Azariah the son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his own house.

verses.kjv: After him repaired Binnui the son of Henadad another piece, from the house of Azariah unto the turning of the wall, even unto the corner.
verses.modern: After him Binnui the son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the Angle and to the corner.

verses.kjv: Palal the son of Uzai, over against the turning of the wall, and the tower which lieth out from the king's high house, that was by the court of the prison. Next unto him Pedaiah the son of Parosh.
verses.modern: Palal the son of Uzai made repairs opposite the Angle and the tower projecting from the upper house of the king at the court of the guard. Next to him Pedaiah the son of Parosh made repairs.

verses.kjv: Moreover the Nethinims dwelt in Ophel, unto the place over against the water gate toward the east, and the tower that lieth out.
verses.modern: The temple servants living on the hill of Ophel made repairs as far as the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.

verses.kjv: After them the Tekoites repaired another piece, over against the great tower that lieth out, even unto the wall of Ophel.
verses.modern: After them the Tekoites repaired another section, opposite the great projecting tower as far as the wall of Ophel.

verses.kjv: From above the horse gate repaired the priests, every one over against his house.
verses.modern: Above the Horse Gate the priests made repairs, each one opposite his own house.

verses.kjv: After them repaired Zadok the son of Immer over against his house. After him repaired also Shemaiah the son of Shechaniah, the keeper of the east gate.
verses.modern: After them Zadok the son of Immer made repairs opposite his own house. After him Shemaiah the son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, made repairs.

verses.kjv: After him repaired Hananiah the son of Shelemiah, and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph, another piece. After him repaired Meshullam the son of Berechiah over against his chamber.
verses.modern: After him Hananiah the son of Shelemiah and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph repaired another section. After him Meshullam the son of Berechiah made repairs opposite his room.

verses.kjv: After him repaired Malchiah the goldsmith's son unto the place of the Nethinims, and of the merchants, over against the gate Miphkad, and to the going up of the corner.
verses.modern: After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and to the upper room of the corner.

verses.kjv: And between the going up of the corner unto the sheep gate repaired the goldsmiths and the merchants.
verses.modern: Between the upper room of the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and merchants made repairs.

chapters.summary: The chapter records the sections of the wall rebuilt by each family, priest, and guild, gate by gate around the circuit of Jerusalem from the Sheep Gate back to the Sheep Gate.

verses.kjv: But it came to pass, that when Sanballat heard that we builded the wall, he was wroth, and took great indignation, and mocked the Jews.
verses.modern: When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was furious and greatly enraged. He ridiculed the Jews,

verses.kjv: And he spake before his brethren and the army of Samaria, and said, What do these feeble Jews? will they fortify themselves? will they sacrifice? will they make an end in a day? will they revive the stones out of the heaps of the rubbish which are burned?
verses.modern: saying before his associates and the army of Samaria, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it by themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish it in a day? Will they revive the stones out of the heaps of rubble — burned ones at that?"

verses.kjv: Now Tobiah the Ammonite was by him, and he said, Even that which they build, if a fox go up, he shall even break down their stone wall.
verses.modern: Tobiah the Ammonite was nearby and said, "Whatever they are building — even a fox could break down their stone wall!"

verses.kjv: Hear, O our God; for we are despised: and turn their reproach upon their own head, and give them for a prey in the land of captivity:
verses.modern: Hear us, our God, for we are despised. Turn their insults back on their own heads. Give them over as plunder in a land of captivity.

verses.kjv: And cover not their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out from before thee: for they have provoked thee to anger before the builders.
verses.modern: Cover not their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out from your sight, for they have thrown insults in the face of the builders.

verses.kjv: So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.
verses.modern: So we rebuilt the wall, and the whole wall was joined together to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.

verses.kjv: But it came to pass, that when Sanballat, and Tobiah, and the Arabians, and the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites, heard that the walls of Jerusalem were made up, and that the breaches began to be stopped, then they were very wroth,
verses.modern: But when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of Jerusalem's walls was progressing and the gaps were being closed, they were very angry.

verses.kjv: And conspired all of them together to come and to fight against Jerusalem, and to hinder it.
verses.modern: They all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and throw it into confusion.

verses.kjv: Nevertheless we made our prayer unto our God, and set a watch against them day and night, because of them.
verses.modern: But we prayed to our God and set a guard as protection against them day and night.

verses.kjv: And Judah said, The strength of the bearers of burdens is decayed, and there is much rubbish; so that we are not able to build the wall.
verses.modern: Then Judah said, "The strength of the laborers is failing; there is so much rubble that we cannot rebuild the wall."

verses.kjv: And our adversaries said, They shall not know, neither see, till we come in the midst among them, and slay them, and cause the work to cease.
verses.modern: Our enemies said, "Before they know it or see us, we will be right among them and kill them and put an end to the work."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when the Jews which dwelt by them came, they said unto us ten times, From all places whence ye shall return unto us they will be upon you.
verses.modern: When the Jews who lived near them came to us, they kept warning us ten times over, "From all the places where they live they will attack us."

verses.kjv: Therefore set I in the lower places behind the wall, and on the higher places, I even set the people after their families with their swords, their spears, and their bows.
verses.modern: So I stationed men in the lower parts of the space behind the wall, in open places. I stationed them by families, with their swords, spears, and bows.

verses.kjv: And I looked, and rose up, and said unto the nobles, and to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, Be not ye afraid of them: remember the LORD, which is great and terrible, and fight for your brethren, your sons, and your daughters, your wives, and your houses.
verses.modern: After looking things over I stood up and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons and daughters, your wives, and your homes."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when our enemies heard that it was known unto us, and God had brought their counsel to nought, that we returned all of us to the wall, every one unto his work.
verses.modern: When our enemies heard that we knew their plot and that God had frustrated it, we all returned to the wall, each to His own work.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass from that time forth, that the half of my servants wrought in the work, and the other half of them held both the spears, the shields, and the bows, and the habergeons; and the rulers were behind all the house of Judah.
verses.modern: From that day on, half of my servants worked on construction while the other half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The officers stood behind the whole house of Judah

verses.kjv: They which builded on the wall, and they that bare burdens, with those that laded, every one with one of his hands wrought in the work, and with the other hand held a weapon.
verses.modern: who were building on the wall. Those who carried loads did their work with one hand holding the load and the other hand holding a weapon.

verses.kjv: For the builders, every one had his sword girded by his side, and so builded. And he that sounded the trumpet was by me.
verses.modern: Each builder wore his sword at his side while he worked. The man who sounded the trumpet stayed close to me.

verses.kjv: And I said unto the nobles, and to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, The work is great and large, and we are separated upon the wall, one far from another.
verses.modern: I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, "The work is extensive and spread out. We are widely separated on the wall, one far from another.

verses.kjv: In what place therefore ye hear the sound of the trumpet, resort ye thither unto us: our God shall fight for us.
verses.modern: Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, rally to us there. Our God will fight for us."

verses.kjv: So we laboured in the work: and half of them held the spears from the rising of the morning till the stars appeared.
verses.modern: So we carried on the work with half of the men holding spears, from the break of dawn until the stars came out.

verses.kjv: Likewise at the same time said I unto the people, Let every one with his servant lodge within Jerusalem, that in the night they may be a guard to us, and labour on the day.
verses.modern: At that time I also told the people, "Let every man and his servant stay inside Jerusalem at night, so that they can stand guard by night and work by day."

verses.kjv: So neither I, nor my brethren, nor my servants, nor the men of the guard which followed me, none of us put off our clothes, saving that every one put them off for washing.
verses.modern: So neither I, nor my brothers, nor my servants, nor the men of the guard who were with me ever took off our clothes, except every one put them off for washing.

chapters.summary: Sanballat and Tobiah mocked the rebuilding and then plotted a military attack; Nehemiah armed the workers and set half the men as guards. The builders worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other, and the work continued day and night.

verses.kjv: And there was a great cry of the people and of their wives against their brethren the Jews.
verses.modern: Now there was a great outcry from the people and their wives against their fellow Jews.

verses.kjv: For there were that said, We, our sons, and our daughters, are many: therefore we take up corn for them, that we may eat, and live.
verses.modern: Some were saying, "We, our sons and daughters, are many. We must get grain so that we can eat and stay alive."

verses.kjv: Some also there were that said, We have mortgaged our lands, vineyards, and houses, that we might buy corn, because of the dearth.
verses.modern: Others were saying, "We are mortgaging our fields, vineyards, and houses to get grain because of the famine."

verses.kjv: There were also that said, We have borrowed money for the king's tribute, and that upon our lands and vineyards.
verses.modern: Still others said, "We have had to borrow money for the king's tax on our fields and vineyards."

verses.kjv: Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children as their children: and, lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters are brought unto bondage already: neither is it in our power to redeem them; for other men have our lands and vineyards.
verses.modern: "Now our flesh is the same as our brothers' flesh; our children are the same as theirs. Yet we are forcing our sons and daughters into slavery. Some of our daughters are already enslaved. We are powerless to help, for our fields and vineyards now belong to others."

verses.kjv: And I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words.
verses.modern: When I heard their outcry and these words, I was very angry.

verses.kjv: Then I consulted with myself, and I rebuked the nobles, and the rulers, and said unto them, Ye exact usury, every one of his brother. And I set a great assembly against them.
verses.modern: After thinking it over, I confronted the nobles and officials and said to them, "You are charging interest on loans to your own brothers!" So I called a great assembly to deal with them.

verses.kjv: And I said unto them, We after our ability have redeemed our brethren the Jews, which were sold unto the heathen; and will ye even sell your brethren? or shall they be sold unto us? Then held they their peace, and found nothing to answer.
verses.modern: I said to them, "We, as best we could, have bought back our fellow Jews who were sold to the nations. But now you are selling your own brothers. They must be bought back by us?" They were silent and could find nothing to say.

verses.kjv: Also I said, It is not good that ye do: ought ye not to walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the heathen our enemies?
verses.modern: So I continued, "What you are doing is not right. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, so that the reproach of our enemies will not fall on us?"

verses.kjv: I likewise, and my brethren, and my servants, might exact of them money and corn: I pray you, let us leave off this usury.
verses.modern: "I myself, my brothers, and my servants are also lending money and grain to the people. But let us stop this practice of charging interest.

verses.kjv: Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, and also the hundredth part of the money, and of the corn, the wine, and the oil, that ye exact of them.
verses.modern: Please give back to them this very day their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses, and also the interest you are charging them — a hundredth of the money, grain, new wine, and olive oil."

verses.kjv: Then said they, We will restore them, and will require nothing of them; so will we do as thou sayest. Then I called the priests, and took an oath of them, that they should do according to this promise.
verses.modern: They replied, "We will restore it and will require nothing more from them. We will do exactly as you say." So I called the priests and made the nobles and officials swear an oath to do what they had promised.

verses.kjv: Also I shook my lap, and said, So God shake out every man from his house, and from his labour, that performeth not this promise, even thus be he shaken out, and emptied. And all the congregation said, Amen, and praised the LORD. And the people did according to this promise.
verses.modern: I also shook out my garment and said, "In this way may God shake out every man from his house and from his property who does not keep this promise. May He be shaken out and emptied!" And all the assembly said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. The people did as they had promised.

verses.kjv: Moreover from the time that I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even unto the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that is, twelve years, I and my brethren have not eaten the bread of the governor.
verses.modern: Furthermore, from the day I was appointed as their governor in the land of Judah — from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, twelve years — neither I nor my brothers ate the food allotted to the governor.

verses.kjv: But the former governors that had been before me were chargeable unto the people, and had taken of them bread and wine, beside forty shekels of silver; yea, even their servants bare rule over the people: but so did not I, because of the fear of God.
verses.modern: The earlier governors who preceded me had placed heavy burdens on the people, taking forty shekels of silver from them for food and wine. Their subordinates also lorded it over the people. But I did not act this way, out of the fear of God.

verses.kjv: Yea, also I continued in the work of this wall, neither bought we any land: and all my servants were gathered thither unto the work.
verses.modern: I also devoted myself to the work on this wall and acquired no land. All my servants were gathered there for the work.

verses.kjv: Moreover there were at my table an hundred and fifty of the Jews and rulers, beside those that came unto us from among the heathen that are about us.
verses.modern: Furthermore, a hundred and fifty Jews and officials ate at my table, in addition to those who came to us from the surrounding nations.

verses.kjv: Now that which was prepared for me daily was one ox and six choice sheep; also fowls were prepared for me, and once in ten days store of all sorts of wine: yet for all this required not I the bread of the governor, because the bondage was heavy upon this people.
verses.modern: Each day one ox, six choice sheep, and birds were prepared for me. Every ten days skins of wine of all kinds were provided. Yet I did not demand the food allotted to the governor, because the burden on these people was already heavy.

verses.kjv: Think upon me, my God, for good, according to all that I have done for this people.
verses.modern: Remember me favorably, my God, for all that I have done for this people.

chapters.summary: The people cried out against the wealthy nobles who were charging interest and seizing their lands and children during the famine. Nehemiah rebuked the nobles, made them return what they had taken, and set an example by refusing the governor’s food allowance for twelve years.

verses.kjv: Now it came to pass, when Sanballat, and Tobiah, and Geshem the Arabian, and the rest of our enemies, heard that I had builded the wall, and that there was no breach left therein; (though at that time I had not set up the doors upon the gates;)
verses.modern: When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and that there was no gap left in it — although at that time I had not yet set the doors in the gates —

verses.kjv: That Sanballat and Geshem sent unto me, saying, Come, let us meet together in some one of the villages in the plain of Ono. But they thought to do me mischief.
verses.modern: Sanballat and Geshem sent a message to me saying, "Come, let us meet together in one of the villages in the plain of Ono." But they intended to harm me.

verses.kjv: And I sent messengers unto them, saying, I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down: why should the work cease, whilst I leave it, and come down to you?
verses.modern: So I sent messengers to them saying, "I am doing a great work and I cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?"

verses.kjv: Yet they sent unto me four times after this sort; and I answered them after the same manner.
verses.modern: They sent the same message to me four times, and each time I sent the same reply.

verses.kjv: Then sent Sanballat his servant unto me in like manner the fifth time with an open letter in his hand;
verses.modern: Sanballat sent his servant to me in the same way a fifth time, with an open letter in his hand.

verses.kjv: Wherein was written, It is reported among the heathen, and Gashmu saith it, that thou and the Jews think to rebel: for which cause thou buildest the wall, that thou mayest be their king, according to these words.
verses.modern: In it was written: "It is reported among the nations — and Geshem confirms it — that you and the Jews are planning to rebel, and that is why you are building the wall. Moreover, according to these reports you intend to become their king.

verses.kjv: And thou hast also appointed prophets to preach of thee at Jerusalem, saying, There is a king in Judah: and now shall it be reported to the king according to these words. Come now therefore, and let us take counsel together.
verses.modern: You have also appointed prophets to proclaim about you in Jerusalem, saying, 'There is a king in Judah!' Now this report will go to the king. So come, let us meet together."

verses.kjv: Then I sent unto him, saying, There are no such things done as thou sayest, but thou feignest them out of thine own heart.
verses.modern: I sent a reply saying, "Nothing of what you say has happened. You are inventing it all yourself."

verses.kjv: For they all made us afraid, saying, Their hands shall be weakened from the work, that it be not done. Now therefore, O God, strengthen my hands.
verses.modern: For they were all trying to frighten us, thinking, "Their hands will drop from the work. It will not be done." But now, O God, strengthen my hands.

verses.kjv: Afterward I came unto the house of Shemaiah the son of Delaiah the son of Mehetabeel, who was shut up; and he said, Let us meet together in the house of God, within the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple: for they will come to slay thee; yea, in the night will they come to slay thee.
verses.modern: Then I went to the house of Shemaiah the son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was confined to his home. He said, "Let us meet together in the house of God, inside the temple, and let us close the temple doors, for they are coming to kill you — indeed, tonight they are coming to kill you."

verses.kjv: And I said, Should such a man as I flee? and who is there, that, being as I am, would go into the temple to save his life? I will not go in.
verses.modern: But I said, "Should a man like me run away? Could someone like me enter the temple to save his life? I will not go in."

verses.kjv: And, lo, I perceived that God had not sent him; but that he pronounced this prophecy against me: for Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
verses.modern: I realized that God had not sent him, but that He had spoken this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired Him.

verses.kjv: Therefore was he hired, that I should be afraid, and do so, and sin, and that they might have matter for an evil report, that they might reproach me.
verses.modern: He was hired to frighten me, so that I would act in this way and sin. Then they could give me a bad reputation and discredit me.

verses.kjv: My God, think thou upon Tobiah and Sanballat according to these their works, and on the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets, that would have put me in fear.
verses.modern: Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these deeds of theirs, and also the prophetess Noadiah and the rest of the prophets who were trying to intimidate me.

verses.kjv: So the wall was finished in the twenty and fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty and two days.
verses.modern: So the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when all our enemies heard thereof, and all the heathen that were about us saw these things, they were much cast down in their own eyes: for they perceived that this work was wrought of our God.
verses.modern: When all our enemies heard of it, all the surrounding nations were afraid and fell greatly in their own estimation, for they saw that this work had been accomplished with the help of our God.

verses.kjv: Moreover in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters unto Tobiah, and the letters of Tobiah came unto them.
verses.modern: Also in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah's letters kept coming to them.

verses.kjv: For there were many in Judah sworn unto him, because he was the son in law of Shechaniah the son of Arah; and his son Johanan had taken the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah.
verses.modern: For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah the son of Arah. His son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah.

verses.kjv: Also they reported his good deeds before me, and uttered my words to him. And Tobiah sent letters to put me in fear.
verses.modern: They also kept telling me about his good deeds and reporting my words to him. And Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.

chapters.summary: Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem tried four times to lure Nehemiah to a meeting to harm him, then hired a false prophet to frighten him into hiding in the temple. Nehemiah refused every trap, and the wall was finished in fifty-two days.

verses.kjv: Now it came to pass, when the wall was built, and I had set up the doors, and the porters and the singers and the Levites were appointed,
verses.modern: When the wall was rebuilt and I had set the doors in place, the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites were appointed.

verses.kjv: That I gave my brother Hanani, and Hananiah the ruler of the palace, charge over Jerusalem: for he was a faithful man, and feared God above many.
verses.modern: I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, along with Hananiah the commander of the fortress, for he was a faithful man who feared God more than many.

verses.kjv: And I said unto them, Let not the gates of Jerusalem be opened until the sun be hot; and while they stand by, let them shut the doors, and bar them: and appoint watches of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, every one in his watch, and every one to be over against his house.
verses.modern: I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened until the sun is hot. While the guards are still on duty, let them shut and bar the doors. Also appoint residents of Jerusalem as guards, some at their posts and some near their own homes."

verses.kjv: Now the city was large and great: but the people were few therein, and the houses were not builded.
verses.modern: Now the city was large and spacious, but the people in it were few and the houses had not yet been rebuilt.

verses.kjv: And my God put into mine heart to gather together the nobles, and the rulers, and the people, that they might be reckoned by genealogy. And I found a register of the genealogy of them which came up at the first, and found written therein,
verses.modern: My God put it into my heart to assemble the nobles, the officials, and the people to be enrolled by genealogy. I found the genealogical record of those who had come up in the first return. I found written in it:

verses.kjv: These are the children of the province, that went up out of the captivity, of those that had been carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away, and came again to Jerusalem and to Judah, every one unto his city;
verses.modern: These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away, and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town:

verses.kjv: Who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah. The number, I say, of the men of Israel was:
verses.modern: They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of Israel:
